description: The figure illustrates five schematic bar-chart patterns labeled “Increasing,” “Uniform,” “Decreasing,” “Spindle,” and “Bottleneck,” intended to represent different distributions of values across a small set of categories. In each mini-chart, the categories are arranged along the horizontal axis as four adjacent bars with no explicit category tick labels, and there is no visible axis label; the vertical axis represents bar height but has no label, numeric ticks, or units, implying an unlabeled linear scale. In the “Increasing” panel, four pale green bars increase from left to right, with the first bar shortest and the fourth tallest. In the “Uniform” panel, four pale green bars are equal height. In the “Decreasing” panel, four pale green bars decrease from left to right, with the first bar tallest and the fourth shortest. In the “Spindle” panel, the first and fourth pale green bars are short while the two middle bars are taller and approximately equal, forming a peak in the center. In the “Bottleneck” panel, the first and fourth pale green bars are taller while the two middle bars are shorter and approximately equal, forming a dip in the center. There is no legend, no stacking or grouping beyond the four bars per panel, and no visual emphasis such as outlines or annotations; within each panel, the bars appear ordered left-to-right to match the named pattern rather than being sorted by a numeric axis.
